overview.text: Bitrefill's partner guide describes wallet-native x402 REST discovery of gift cards, eSIMs and mobile top-ups, invoicing, payment and delivery checks, distinct from OAuth/API-key MCP integration. Per-request USDC micro-fees of $0.001-$0.002 can be waived through wallet sign-in, not the product invoice amount. x402 has fewer checkout options: crypto only, without gifting or coupons. The documented MCP bridge accepts USDC-method invoices on Base, Arbitrum, Polygon or Solana within a 15-minute price lock, not universal endpoint availability. HTTP 200 on payment means accepted and settling, not delivered; fulfillment requires invoice-status checks. Redemption codes require authentication as the paying wallet. Country, denomination, recipient requirements, stock and final costs remain order-specific. Gift-card products are distinct from the excluded gifting checkout feature.
